content.text:
No. [PR 1271](https://github.com/iqb-berlin/testcenter/pull/1271) broadly implements the described flow, but it does not reliably provide the claimed protection and contains unrelated behavior changes.

Critical findings:

- Proof-of-work is bypassable. ALTCHA signatures use hardcoded `SystemConfig::$server_key = 'Secret'`. An attacker can forge an easy challenge and submit it directly to `PUT /session`. Secret must be deployment-specific and private.
- Admin login is broken when protection is disabled. `BackendService.adminLogin()` was changed to call `login()`, therefore `/session/login`, instead of `/session/admin`.
- Existing authentication-cache behavior was silently removed:
  - `CacheService::removeAuthentication()`
  - `CacheService::storeAuthentication()`
  
  This affects both automatic person-session creation and code login. Description only calls this an extraction; it does not disclose the behavior removal.
- Existing failed-login limits were removed globally, including when proof-of-work is disabled. The description explains replacing them, but configuration promises an unprotected legacy flow when disabled. That legacy flow now has neither delay nor attempt limit.
- Admin error response leaks the submitted password:
  `Challenge for this password(\`$password\`) ...`
- Empty code submission changed from doing nothing to calling `codeLogin('')`. Unrelated behavior change.
- Admin return-route handling was added. Useful perhaps, but unrelated and not named by any explicit feature/refactor commit.
- ALTCHA is statically imported and the whole package copied into deployment assets. This contradicts the PR’s own outstanding lazy-loading review TODO.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` entry, contrary to repository PR rules.

Missing tests:

- Forged/invalid challenge rejection.
- Enabled versus disabled configuration behavior.
- Direct legacy endpoint blocking.
- Person challenge authentication and completion.
- Replay behavior.
- Authentication-cache preservation.
- Frontend endpoint selection—this would likely have caught the admin-login regression.

Commit scope:

- The three principal Infra/BE/FE commits match the advertised feature.
- Fix commits cover formatting/tests and a duplicated function.
- Three merge commits introduced/confounded additional changes.
- No commit explicitly authorizes a refactor beyond extracting login methods.

Recommendation: do not merge or cherry-pick wholesale. Minimal implementation should preserve existing login/cache behavior, add only the challenge gate, use a private configured signing key, retain legacy protection when PoW is disabled, and cherry-pick/rebuild the feature commits without merge-derived UI changes.
